source: Author requested five armor types with separate chest, legs, boots, arms and helmet entries, October 15, 2026. Plasteel, iron and chitin were requested examples; steel and ceramic-faced armor complete this first brainstorm. Docs/WORLD_BASIS.md controls material and ancient-recovery boundaries.
scope: 25 individual piece records across five design families. No whole-set inventory record, automatic full-set grant, set bonus, gameplay equipment slots, world placement, streaming or saved runtime deltas.

defaults.Carrier metadata: Booter-worn armor concept; fitting, packing and spare-cargo rules unresolved.
defaults.Acquisition: Proposed contemporary fabrication or specialist trade; construction recipe unresolved.
defaults.Crafting / processing: Separate fitted piece using selected qualified stock; no whole-set recipe, quantities, yield or production time authored.
defaults.Limitations: Fit, coverage, articulation, mass, durability and protection remain proposals. No wood, ordinary cloth, free-water quenching, set bonuses or new equipment slots.
defaults.Classification basis: One independently listed armor piece. Family membership is a design grouping, never another inventory item or a set bonus.
defaults.Tier basis: Proposed finished-piece planning tier; recipe and properties unresolved.

items.name: Iron chestplate
items.purpose: Iron armor family: individually listed chestplate. Torso and upper back; a chest piece does not include arm or leg pieces. Broad worked-iron plates with plain rolled edges and exposed metal fasteners. Construction and protection are proposals; the five family pieces remain separate items.
items.icon: Iron chestplate: Broad worked-iron plates with plain rolled edges and exposed metal fasteners. Show only this piece, not a complete armor suit.

items.name: Ancient plasteel chestplate
items.purpose: Extremely rare recovered ancient plasteel chestplate, listed as one separate armor item. Torso and upper back; a chest piece does not include arm or leg pieces. Recovered pale composite segments with unfamiliar recessed fittings, wear and mismatched surviving surfaces. Presence does not establish contemporary manufacture or a usable fitted piece.
